title: UAE Secretly Struck Iran During War, WSJ Reports
excerpt: Abu Dhabi hit a key Persian Gulf refinery in April, joining the US and Israel as an active combatant — without saying a word publicly.
body:
Abu Dhabi launched covert military strikes inside Iran during the Gulf war, the *Wall Street Journal* reported on May 12, making the UAE the first Gulf Arab state publicly implicated as an active combatant alongside the US and Israel. The operation marks a seismic shift in how the Emirates confronts Tehran.

**What happened:**
The strikes — which Abu Dhabi has not publicly acknowledged — included an airstrike on Iran's Lavan Island refinery in the Persian Gulf in early April, timed close to President Trump's ceasefire announcement. The attack ignited a large fire and knocked much of the facility's roughly 55,000-barrel-per-day processing capacity offline for months. Iran acknowledged at the time that an 'enemy' had hit the site, then retaliated by firing missiles and drones at the UAE and Kuwait.

**Why Abu Dhabi acted — and why Washington looked away:**
The UAE had every reason for fury. Iran fired more than 2,800 missiles and drones at the Emirates throughout the conflict — more than any other country in the region, including Israel. Washington, sources told the Journal, was not troubled by the Emirati strike because the ceasefire had not yet formally taken hold, and quietly welcomed Gulf state participation. The UAE's Foreign Ministry declined to comment on the strikes but pointed to prior statements asserting its right to respond militarily to hostile acts. The Pentagon also declined to comment.

**What to watch:**
With the ceasefire still fragile and Iran reportedly ramping up strikes again, markets and diplomats will closely track whether Abu Dhabi acknowledges its role — and whether Tehran escalates further against Emirati energy and trade infrastructure.
